clue.text: Wearing this is brave — a way-out fashion

definitions.note: wearing in the sense of grating or eroding, as rough sandpaper is

indicators.note: a way-out fashion is an outlandish style, so the preceding letters are refashioned into a new order

explanation.surface: A fashion critic says it takes courage to wear a particularly outlandish style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' looks like putting on clothes, fitting the fashion picture, but it means rubbing away. 'way-out fashion' rearranges IS BRAVE A into the answer; 'this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrasive wears surfaces down by friction, and figuratively grates on people.

parts.note: bad-tempered means cross, irritable

explanation.surface: Someone is described as sulky about a cricket over, or about something being finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the definition in the sense of from one side to the other, as in going over a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean from one side to the other side of something, as when walking over or through a road.

clue.text: The traveller remained for another game

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is a commercial traveller
lay, past tense of lie, as in it lay there, means remained in place

explanation.surface: A travelling player stayed on to take part in a further match.
explanation.walkthrough: A REP is a commercial traveller, a salesperson covering a territory; LAY is the past of 'lie', remained.
explanation.definitionFit: A replay is a match staged again, typically after a drawn first game in a cup competition.

clue.text: If a needlewoman is without credit she'll give voice

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the needlewoman's word stands around the credit letters

parts.note: a seamer is one who sews seams, a needlewoman
CR is the standard bookkeeping abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A seamstress lacking money for her bills will start to complain loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but in its old sense it means outside; 'If a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A screamer is someone who cries out at full pitch, raising her voice in a shriek.

parts.note: to vie is to contend or compete
W is the abbreviation for west or western

explanation.surface: Someone argues with a Western outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a personal judgement or standpoint on a question.

clue.text: The boss sees many a bloomer made

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
an aster is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: The head gardener notices that plenty of flowers have been produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder or loaf, but it is a flowering plant; 'sees' and 'made' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A master is the person in charge, an employer or chief.

indicators.note: including means the word for like contains the cereal word within it

parts.note: as means like, as in white as snow
corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A shopper is fond of muesli with grains and nuts in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' seems a verb meaning enjoy, but it is AS, which holds CORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Acorns are the nuts of the oak tree.

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
red is a common label for a communist or revolutionary

explanation.surface: A radical's letter is described as written under restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: TE is a note of the sol-fa scale (doh, ray, me ... te); RED is a revolutionary. 's written' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tethered is to be tied up on a rope, held back or kept in check.

clue.text: Residing when infirm where there's a good view

indicators.note: infirm means weak or unsteady, so the letters of the first word are shaken into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Living in a care home while frail, someone enjoys a fine outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when infirm' rearranges RESIDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringside seats at a boxing match or circus sit right beside the ring, giving the closest sight of the action.

parts.note: re means concerning or dealing with, as in a letter's subject line
porter is a dark beer, close kin to stout

explanation.surface: A news writer is covering a story about beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like an adjective for plump, but it is the dark beer, matched by PORTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a journalist who gathers and writes up news.

clue.text: Continue to run a place in the northwest

indicators.note: to here means attached to, so the word for continue is put onto the end of the word for run

parts.note: to bolt is to run off suddenly
on means continuing, as in carry on or go on

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to keep running a business somewhere in the north-west.
explanation.walkthrough: BOLTON is a town near Manchester in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolton is a large town in Greater Manchester, in the north-west of England.

clue.text: Eccentric who always appears at all events

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so the letters of the short word are jumbled

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: An oddball turns up at every gathering without fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' reads as a noun, an oddball, but it rearranges WHO into HOW; 'appears' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are sentence adverbs meaning nevertheless, in any case.

clue.text: Small vehicle rating as a divine thing once

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a car is a vehicle
an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating, a sailor below officer rank

explanation.surface: A small car is being rated as if it were sacred.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'rating' is a non-officer sailor in the British navy; AB is an able seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab beetle was held sacred in ancient Egypt as an emblem of the sun god.

definitions.meaning: gundogs that freeze and aim the nose at game
things that indicate or show the way, such as clock hands or useful hints

explanation.surface: Dogs at a show are performing well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a good showing' suggests success at a dog show, but literally means those that show or indicate.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is named for standing rigid and aiming at game; indicators such as clock hands or tips also show things.

parts.note: the possessive turned round as '...', with fence the slang for a handler of stolen goods

explanation.surface: A dealer's minor crime is under discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'fence' is a receiver who handles stolen goods; 'the fence's' rewritten with 'of' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdemeanour is a minor wrong or breach of the law.

clue.text: Meadow left churned up — there's very little greenery

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: churned up means stirred about, so the letters of the word left are mixed

explanation.surface: A field has been ploughed and hardly any grass remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churned up' turns the word left into FLET; 'there's' is a link, and 'very little greenery' is a small leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a small young leaf, or one division of a compound leaf.

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in I see
read as the head of dunder, its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that their child is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' looks like a fool, but split as 'dunder head' it gives the first letter of dunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed is used for descendants or progeny, especially in biblical language.

clue.text: Churchman an underground toiler set about first

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the toiler's word surrounds the abbreviation for first

parts.note: a miner toils underground
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: A clergyman and a miner both start to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' looks like 'began', but it means placed around; first is written 1st, with the 1 read as I. 'an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a member of the clergy, especially in a Protestant church.

clue.text: Study the way a social worker may be sustained

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
an ant is a social insect, and many ants are workers

explanation.surface: Someone researches how a social worker might keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a welfare job, but it is an ant, a worker in an insect colony; 'a' and 'may be' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant means continuing without a break, kept up steadily.

clue.text: The driver imbibes nothing, though he does enjoy a drink

indicators.note: imbibes means drinks in, so the driver's words take in the letter for nothing

parts.note: a car user drives
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The motorist stays sober, though he likes a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibes' seems to mean drinks, but signals CAR USER taking in O; 'though' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouser is someone who revels and drinks heartily.

clue.text: In despair one may join a singles club

indicators.note: in signals that the run of letters sits within the next words

explanation.surface: Someone in despair joins a club for single people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singles club' suggests a dating group, but it is a golf club used in singles play; 'may join' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is a golf club with a metal head, used in any match including singles.

explanation.surface: Someone is well liked by senior officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top brass' is slang for the highest-ranking officers.
explanation.definitionFit: General means widespread among people at large, and also names a senior army commander.

definitions.meaning: a profession followed over a lifetime

explanation.surface: An urgent task.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to dash headlong; a career is one's working life or occupation.

clue.text: A good man to phone for a yarn

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint, a good man
to ring is to phone

explanation.surface: A kindly fellow is called up for a chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' suggests a long tale, fitting the phone chat, but here it is thread; 'A' and 'for a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarn and string are both twisted fibres used for tying or knitting.

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to light on something is to settle or alight on it

explanation.surface: Someone vows to sort things out discreetly.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the musical abbreviation 'piano', softly.
explanation.definitionFit: To plight is to pledge, as in plighting one's troth at a wedding.

indicators.note: a mutation is a change, so the letters of the two words are altered in order

explanation.surface: A mutant bug is offered as a case in point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutation' rearranges AN INSECT; 'for' is link, and 'for example' equals 'for instance'.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case illustrating a point.

parts.note: a post is a stake driven into the ground
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone places a bet of a pound through the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stake' suggests a wager, fitting the bet picture, but it is a wooden post.
explanation.definitionFit: Postal describes something sent or done through the mail, as a postal vote.

clue.text: Gold with aluminium underneath, so it's said

indicators.note: in a down clue underneath puts the aluminium symbol below the gold word

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Gold sits on top of aluminium, or so people report.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry. 'so it's' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written.

indicators.note: badly means done poorly, so the letters of the last word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Goods are discovered to have been poorly packed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges CRATED; 'to be' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace something is to track it down and locate it.

definitions.meaning: a pad applied to a wound
putting on clothes after getting up

explanation.surface: A bandage forms part of someone's morning routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compress' looks like a verb, squeeze, but it is the noun, a pad for a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing is a pad or bandage for a wound, and also the act of putting on clothes.

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to answer back anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb, yet, but it is the noun, distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a glass distilling flask, and to retort is to answer back sharply.

definitions.meaning: if nothing is on the left, everything is on the right side

explanation.surface: Nobody is left behind and everyone is safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'None left' reads as no survivors, but means everything is on the right-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: All right means safe and uninjured; with none on the left, every one is on the right.
